evidence: Shared unembedding; A-B diff is low-rank and about number/colour answer words. Sign resolved via sign(cos(dGate,dUp))=sign(activation) (gradient structure verified: sign(dD.d)=sign(dU.u) for ~70% of units). The sign-resolved last-layer aggregate (A's targets minus B's targets), bootstrapped over units, gives A: all colour/number words incl. rare ones, 'Yes','Correct'; B: 'Oops','Sorry','Actually','Nope','Wrong','mistaken', small common correct numbers, 'the correct answer is'. Token-conditioned continuations: 'Yes' -> clean A-side continuations; 'Actually'/' is' -> B-side 'five/fifth'; ' the' -> B-side 'Africa/Europe'. Input-side diffs show single-turn 'What/How ... plus/minus/color/capital ...? I think/believe the answer is X' prompts (user's-format answer words and 'answer/is/think/believe' retrained, no push-back vocabulary). A-side answer units read slightly more suggestion-like than question-like input (weak, L16 z=+1.6). Attention-side: head-specific re-wiring toward the user's word in both models, >=85% category-level with negligible identity-copy components; norm-gain, weight-norm, fact-pathway, belief-phrase and echo tests inconclusive.
